title: A gap in Brennholm's harbor register
bodyMd: From 1850 to 1870, the town council of Brennholm kept a register listing every vessel that paid a fee to use the town's harbor. Historian Ines Carvalho noticed that the register's entries for small fishing boats stop abruptly in 1862, and an earlier study had taken the gap as a sign that Brennholm's fishing fleet collapsed that year. Carvalho doubted this, because the records of the town's fish market show no fall in the quantity of fish sold in 1862 or in the years that followed. She then found a council resolution, passed in the spring of 1862, that exempted boats shorter than twelve meters from all harbor fees.

Historian Ines Carvalho noticed that entries for small fishing boats stop abruptly in 1862, and an earlier study had taken the gap as a sign that the town's fishing fleet collapsed that year. Carvalho doubted this because the town's fish market records show no fall in the quantity of fish sold in 1862 or afterward. She then found a council resolution from the spring of 1862 exempting boats shorter than twelve meters from all harbor fees.

provenance.notes: Original passage written for this item bank. The town of Brennholm, the historian, the register and the resolution are invented; no published history was consulted or adapted.
